verdict_line: A US$788M carrier mid-way through a cloud TMS replacement, with a cross-border intermodal agreement with CPKC — another customer. Two roster accounts, one lane, and a new platform to integrate around.

thesis.text: Scale is established. Revenue of US$788.4 million per the Transport Topics for-hire ranking (data through 31 December 2025) — Transport Topics reports in US dollars, so this is roughly C$1.05–1.1 billion. Bison operates 2,000+ tractors and around 10,000 trailers and containers with roughly 4,000 employees and contractors.

A TMS replacement is under way. Bison partnered with Mastery Logistics Systems to implement the cloud-based MasterMind TMS, announced April 2025, and added barcode technology for real-time freight updates in March 2025.

The CPKC intermodal agreement links two customers. Bison signed with Canadian Pacific Kansas City for continuous cross-border intermodal service across Canada, the US and Mexico — the intermodal horizontal made literal.

Leadership changed in 2024. Mike Ludwick is President and CEO, effective 1 June 2024, succeeding Rob Penner who retired 31 May 2024. Chairman Don Streuber, COO Steve Zokvic, CFO Hans Andersen. Note: some third-party profiles still name other individuals as CEO and are wrong.

exhibits.title: Scale and the TMS programme
exhibits.headline: US$788 million of revenue and a cloud TMS implementation in flight — integration work with a defined anchor.
exhibits.body_html:
Bison is a privately held, asset-based carrier founded in 1969, headquartered in Winnipeg, acquired by James Richardson and Sons in January 2021. It operates terminals, warehouses and yards across Canada, the United States and Mexico, and owns H.O. Wolding, trading as Bison Transport USA. Revenue of US$788,404 thousand is reported in the Transport Topics for-hire carrier ranking using data through 31 December 2025 — the 2024 ranking showed roughly US$1.0 billion, and CEO Rob Penner told CBC around the 2021 acquisition that revenues were in the range of $850 million.

Group size is genuinely uncertain. The ranked entity covers Bison plus H.O. Wolding, and it is not clear whether Britton, Hartt, Searcy or Pottle's are consolidated into it. James Richardson and Sons publishes no consolidated statements, so a group figure materially above US$1 billion cannot be verified from any public source — but nor can it be ruled out. Confirm actual group revenue through the account relationship before quoting a number to anyone.

The company markets specifically to technology and semiconductor shippers, citing GPS tracking, geofencing, carrier vetting, controlled yard processes and real-time visibility for high-value time-sensitive freight, plus dedicated fleet solutions for just-in-time semiconductor supply and data-centre deployment projects.
exhibits.sowhat: A new cloud TMS is the single best time to engage: integration, data migration, analytics and AI layers are all specified in the first eighteen months after go-live. Patient family-conglomerate ownership supports multi-year platform investment.

exhibits.title: The CPKC lane
exhibits.headline: A cross-border intermodal agreement with CPKC connects two Mphasis accounts through one lane.
exhibits.body_html: Bison announced an agreement with Canadian Pacific Kansas City (February 2024) to provide continuous cross-border intermodal service through Canada, the United States and Mexico. CPKC is also a Mphasis customer, making this the only place on the roster where two accounts share an operating lane.
exhibits.sowhat: Cross-border intermodal is a data problem before it is a rail or truck problem — customs, three regulatory regimes, equipment interchange, handoff visibility. Bison and CPKC each own one half of that lane and neither owns the data that joins it. One capability, two relationships.

financials.basis: Transport Topics for-hire carrier rankings, reported in US DOLLARS. Covers the ranked entity (Bison Transport plus H.O. Wolding dba Bison Transport USA); it is not clear the ranking consolidates Britton, Hartt, Searcy or Pottle's. Bison publishes no audited financials and James Richardson and Sons publishes no consolidated statements.
